summary.name: Understanding Midjourney Prompt Combinations and Weights
summary.one_liner: A Google Docs guide documenting experiments on how Midjourney handles separators, prompt weights, negative weights, image weights, upscaling flags, aspect ratios and seeds, using a Utah Teapot baseline.
use_cases: Learning how Midjourney weights and blends prompt terms
Choosing image weight values for image prompts
Testing how separators affect a Midjourney prompt
Comparing aspect ratio and seed effects on output
Reducing grain when upscaling with --uplight and --stop
summary.what_it_does: The document is a set of informal experiments run in Midjourney using a Utah Teapot image prompt and the word Wood as a baseline. It tests whether different separator characters change results, finding that most have little effect, and shows how double-colon prompt weights blend concepts and how negative weights behave. It also covers image weight (--iw) values from 0.1 to 100, the effect of --stop and --uplight on upscaling, aspect ratio changes with --ar, and how seed values vary output. Most result images are in tables that did not survive into the text, so conclusions are mainly the author's written observations.
notable: Systematic side-by-side tests of separators, weights, and seeds on one fixed image prompt
Documents negative weight behavior and the rule that weights must sum to a non-negative total
Notes the page has moved to a new Google Sites address
caveats: Result images are in tables that are not captured in the page text, so many findings cannot be verified here
The author notes the tests did not use --sameseed, so seed comparisons are less controlled
The page says it has moved to a new location
